data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the same 4 files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, efr-code.install, LICENSE). The deepseek model correctly identified all files as safe: PKGBUILD has no executable code in global scope and uses pinned SHA-256 checksums for upstream binaries; the install script only prints informational messages with no automated execution; .SRCINFO is standard metadata; LICENSE is plain text. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was caused by an HTTP 400 API error when reviewing .SRCINFO, not by any security concern. No injection patterns, no dynamic code execution, no network requests during build/install, and no obfuscation were found.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 API failure) in the qwen model when reviewing .SRCINFO, not by differing security assessments. The deepseek model successfully reviewed .SRCINFO and found it to be standard metadata with pinned checksums. Both models agreed on the safety of the other 3 files.

learnings: API errors on individual files should not cause the entire audit to be marked inconclusive when other files are successfully reviewed and found safe - implement graceful degradation
